title: Remove the size-of-the-move setting cleanly
description:
## As asked

Repository: JKershaw/LinearViewer (Harbour).

**What this is for.** LIN-4346 added the "Size of the move" setting in Settings › Running. John found it unusable: "The setting makes zero sense for someone who doesn't know specifics of how Harbour works … It asks a mandatory question without doing the work to explain the question." He also didn't see its purpose "given we'll give users a per task breakdown of options to choose from." He called it "obviously wrong and a mistake." His call: "I'd be happy to remove the feature cleanly."

**What we want.** The setting is gone, cleanly. Harbour keeps running hands-off ("A default option for hands off operation is fine"), behaving as it does now with the value John chose, "err larger". Tidying that falls out of the removal is fine. Anything else goes to the area notes, not to new tickets.

**Not this ticket:** "we add settings to the list for discussion." The operator records that separately.

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself, and record why. Raise a ruling only for John's calls: how big a move is, what's spent, removing a step, the order of work, and authority.

**Done when** Settings no longer offers the setting, a task runs hands-off without asking about size, and nothing that existed only for the setting remains.

*End of what was asked. Steps write below this line; nothing above it changes.*

## Size of the move

**Size:** just the task
**Why:** Removes the setting and everything that existed only for it, keeps hands-off running fixed at err larger, and leaves old history readable but not undoable; John ruled the removal done cleanly and no wider.
**Cuts:** none
**Decided by:** a ruling

## Implementation Plan

*Pruned at close-out, 8 Nov 2026.* The plan, its research and the scoping sections are discharged. The full history is in the task snapshots (the last pre-prune one is from 15:47 UTC on 8 Nov) and in the comment trail.

## Outcome

Implemented in [PR #2377](<https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2377>), squash-merged as `393c7686b` and deployed on [harbour.cat](<http://harbour.cat>).

* The setting is gone from Settings › Running, along with its route, loader, setter, Undo sink and context plumbing. Running reads `Runner ready` / `No runner`.
* Scoping renders the built-in err-larger standing policy at every entrance. The standing policy still never decides a cut.
* John's old change-log row still reads but can't be undone. The store refuses any retired setting with `NOT_UNDOABLE`. `preferences.sizePolicy` stays stored and unread, with no migration.
* The plan was implemented as approved, with one deviation, recorded beside the ceiling: measured, the empty-context scoping budget rose 29 bytes instead of falling, while the real hands-off render fell 94.
* Leftovers are Waiting entries in `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`. Two post-deploy checks were not run (the live Settings page, and the next live scoping record). They are listed in the close-out comment and on the PR.

### Session and review

fits one session.

comments.body:
## Survey open-0: LIN-4393 @ f0388614c

**Why this will be harder than "delete a settings row"**

1. **Deleting the setting turns on the behaviour John objected to.** `DEFAULT_SIZE_POLICY` is `'ask'` (`lib/size-of-move.js:104`). If you take out the stored preference and its loader, `formatSizePolicyLine` falls back to "no standing policy; the size of the move is a person's ruling". The scoping prompt then says "Without one, the size is pending a ruling: raise it as a `DECISION:`" (`lib/prompt-template-defs.js`, scoping). So every ticket would stop for a size ruling, which is the opposite of hands-off. The removal has to fix err-larger as the only behaviour. Scoping's ask/no-ask branch then folds into one line, and `docs/plans/survey.md` ("How the choice is made", the `ask` bullet) has to change to match.

2. **Know where "the setting" ends.** The setting is `sizePolicy`: its preference, `loadSizePolicy`/`setSizePolicy`, the Settings row, `POST …/running/size-policy`, its change-log entry and Undo sink, the `Ready · larger / ask` state in `settings-areas.js`, the "Size policy set" row, and the policy line passed through four prompt call sites (`dispatch-entrance.js:1591`, `proxy-compute.js:288,443`, `workspace-api-prompts.js:248`). The **size record** (`## Size of the move`, the proxy's `SIZE_RECORD_*` guard, the look-first route, scoping itself) is a separate thing. It is not there "only for the setting". Removing it means removing a step, which is John's call, and his "per task breakdown of options" suggests the per-task choice stays. Keep `DECIDED_BY.policy` ("the standing policy") as it is: records already on tickets carry it, and `readSizeRecord` parses it. Keep `SIZE_RECORD_POLICY_CUT` too, because a built-in policy still must never decide a cut.

3. **Old change-log rows can still be undone.** `undoable` is true for any `kind: 'change'` row (`workspace-change-log.js:184`). If the `sizePolicy` sink is removed from the undo route, Undo on the existing row (John's err-larger change) falls through to `setWorkspaceFeature({ featureKey: 'sizePolicy' })` (`routes/settings.js:580`). That writes a junk feature flag, or at best fails with a misleading CONFLICT. Old rows still need to render (keep a summary line) but must not be undoable. Taking `'sizePolicy'` out of `SETTINGS` blocks new writes, which is correct, but nothing reads that list on the way out.

4. **The stored value is left behind.** `preferences.sizePolicy` stays in the store. Once nothing reads it, it's harmless. Leave it and say so; no migration.

5. **The wider footprint.** `llms.txt`, `proxy-instructions.js`, the architecture docs, the scoping byte budget, a prompt change-log entry, and about eight test files. The router fixtures show the record fact, not the policy, so they stay as they are. The evidence docs are history; leave them alone.

**The deeper point.** John's complaint, "a mandatory question without doing the work to explain the question", fits the record's vocabulary just as well ("consolidate the decision this task touches") and the pending-ruling path for cuts. Removing the setting doesn't touch either. That belongs in the area notes, not this ticket.

**What I'd do first.** Write the regression test before deleting anything. It should check that the scoping prompt, rendered with no policy context on every path, still says err-larger, and that an old `sizePolicy` change-log row renders but offers no Undo. Then remove the setting from the outside in: Settings UI and route, then the change log, then the loader plumbing, then the docs.

## Survey global: LIN-4393 @ f0388614c

**Where it lands.** The setting is a thin knob, `sizePolicy` (`ask` | `err-larger`), on top of a large, new and still-moving body: the size record in `lib/size-of-move.js` (four replay arms in two days). The knob runs through:
- `lib/size-of-move.js`: `SIZE_POLICIES`, `DEFAULT_SIZE_POLICY = 'ask'`, `POLICY_MEANING`, `formatSizePolicyLine`
- `lib/workspace-preferences.js`: `loadSizePolicy`, `setSizePolicy`, and the classification comment
- five call sites that pass `context.sizePolicy` along: `dispatch-entrance.js`, `recommendation-input.js`, `routes/workspace-api-prompts.js`, and `routes/proxy-compute.js` twice
- Settings: `routes/settings.js` (the POST route and an Undo sink), `render-settings-workspace.js` (a row, a "set" row, an undo row), `settings-areas.js` (`features`, `routes`, the sidebar state "Ready · larger"), and `workspace-change-log.js` (`SETTINGS`, `SIZE_POLICY_WORDS`)
- four tests, `docs/plans/survey.md` §How the choice is made, `source-map.md`

The record itself (the heading, `SIZES`, `DECIDED_BY`, `checkSizeRecord`, the look-first route) does not depend on the setting.

**The trap if it's done the obvious way.** The code default is `ask`, and `ask` means "every size is a ruling; the record reads pending until a person answers". Hands-off running today comes only from John's stored `err-larger` (set 7 Nov). If you delete the setting and keep the fallback, Harbour silently goes from hands-off to waiting on a person for every task. Tests that only check Settings would still pass. What survives has to be **the policy fixed at err-larger**, not "no policy". Then `formatSizePolicyLine` becomes a constant (one string, no `setAt`), and the five call sites stop passing it along. Pin the err-larger wording with a test that passes no context.

**What else has to learn about the removal.**
- *Census:* `settings-areas` `features` is checked against `SETTINGS` (census test :44), and its `routes` against the real routes, so both lists have to change together.
- *Old change-log rows* (the history, not the Settings page): `record()` refuses unknown settings, but rows already stored with `setting: 'sizePolicy'` stay in the log. Without the sink, an Undo on one falls through to the workspace-feature fallback and gets refused with a misleading "conflict". Without `SIZE_POLICY_WORDS`, the summary reads "sizePolicy changed". Keep a read-only summary for old rows and make them not undoable, or decide on purpose to drop them.
- *Stored preference:* `preferences.sizePolicy` stays in Mongo, unread. Harmless; leave it or unset it, but say which.
- *Prompt bytes:* scoping shrinks, so `prompt-size-budget.test.js` and `scripts/prompt-template-change-log.md` need an entry.
- *Not setting-only, so keep:* `DECIDED_BY.policy` ("the standing policy"), `SIZE_RECORD_POLICY_CUT`, and the `pending` path for cuts. The policy outlives the knob. Deleting these as "policy stuff" would remove the guard that keeps a policy from deciding "wrong work".

**Better, at a cost this task can carry.** Remove the policy *setting* and keep the policy *meaning* as one exported constant in `size-of-move.js`. The scoping line and the plan doc then read from one place. Rewrite `docs/plans/survey.md`'s three bullets as two: the policy decides larger or just-the-task, and a cut gets a ruling. Also drop the "ask" branch from `formatSizePolicyLine`.

**Better still, not this task's.** John's other remark ("we'll give users a per task breakdown of options") points past the knob: the whole idea of a "standing policy" may be standing in for a per-task choice that doesn't exist yet. Revisit `DECIDED_BY.policy` then; that goes in the area notes.

## Size of the move (the person's call)

The removal, done cleanly, and no wider. John: "I'd be happy to remove the feature cleanly."

**The trap.** Hands-off running depends only on John's stored value. Without it, the built-in fallback is "ask", which stops every task. Afterwards, err larger must be how Harbour behaves.

**What goes:** the setting and everything that exists only for it.

**What stays:** the size record on each ticket and the look-first route. They are not the setting.

**Old history:** John's change-log row must still read. Say in the pull request what happens to the stored value.

**To the area notes:** John's remark about "a per task breakdown of options".

**Questions:** settle engineering questions yourself, and record why. Raise a ruling only for John's calls: how big a move is, what's spent, removing a step, the order of work, and authority.

**Done when** Settings no longer offers the setting, a test shows a task with no stored value runs hands-off leaning larger, John's old change-log row still reads and offers nothing broken, and nothing that existed only for the setting remains.

## Implementation: PR open, CI green

**PR:** https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2377 (head `70e0fcfa5`, rebased onto `3272fe4a6`). `ci-success` is green: unit tests, all 4 E2E shards and the secret scan passed.

**What landed** (as planned, one PR)
- The policy is now built in: `STANDING_POLICY_LINE` in `lib/size-of-move.js` is the err-larger line, without the setting date. Scoping renders it on every path, and its no-policy `DECISION:` clause is gone. The cut sentence is unchanged, so the policy still never decides a cut.
- Removed the setting and everything that existed only for it: the Settings row, the "set" row, its Undo row, the POST route and its undo sink; the loader and setter; the recommendation-input field; and the policy loads at all five scoping entrances. Running reads `Runner ready` / `No runner` again.
- Old change-log rows still read ("Size of the move: err larger") but can't be undone. The change-log store refuses a retired setting with `NOT_UNDOABLE` before either callback runs.
- `preferences.sizePolicy` is left stored and unread. No migration.
- Kept: the size record, `DECIDED_BY` (all three values), every `SIZE_RECORD_*` guard, the cut-ruling path, the look-first route and the selector fact.

**Where the plan's prediction didn't hold.** The plan expected scoping's prompt ceiling to go down. Measured, it goes up by 29. The budget fixture stores no policy, so it used to render the short "no standing policy" line and now renders the err-larger line. The render a hands-off workspace actually gets falls by 94 bytes. The reason is recorded beside the ceiling. Defs −103, total −74.

**Witnesses** (written first, red at the base). Every scoping entrance renders err larger, both with no stored value and with a stored `ask` (7/7 failed at the base). Settings no longer offers the setting, and the old route returns 404. John's seeded row reads with no Undo, and a forged undo returns `not_undoable` with nothing written. A store-level case confirms the refusal happens before `readCurrent` or `apply`. The cut guard test passes unchanged.

**Local suite:** 24665/24666 pass. The one failure is `scripts/code-shape/wrappers.test.mjs` (acorn). It fails the same way on `main` in this sandbox and has nothing to do with this change; CI passes it.

**Area notes:** a new Waiting entry in `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md` (citing `lib/size-of-move.js`) records John's "per task breakdown of options" point and the unexplained size and cut questions. Existing entries were tightened to fit the byte cap, and none were dropped.

**Cuts to the As-asked block:** none.

### Leftovers

PR: https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2377, head `0e81c6c2c8d9535eee124d3d60bd5c107aba75ce`. `ci-success` is green on that head (unit tests, 4 E2E shards, secret scan).

- **Noted:** the pinned-kind and in-app scoping renders (`lib/dispatch-entrance.js`, `routes/proxy-compute.js` twice, `routes/workspace-api-prompts.js`) each build the prompt context by hand instead of going through `prepareRecommendationInput`, so a new field has to reach five places. LIN-4368's field missed one until review. Added as a Waiting entry in `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, citing `lib/recommendation-input.js`.
- **Tidied:** a comment this change made untrue. The scoping-pointer Waiting entry said to do the work "in the next change to scoping's prompt". This change was one, and it left that work out because the size of the move was just the task. The entry now says so.
- **For close-out:** nothing.

Lessons added:
- `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`: the budget fixture passes no context, so it measures a prompt's empty-context branch. Dropping a branch can raise a ceiling even while real renders shrink, so measure instead of predicting (the plan predicted wrongly here).
- `docs/areas/auth-accounts-and-workspaces.md` (new note): to retire a logged setting, take it out of `SETTINGS` and keep its summary words. Removing only the undo sink lets old rows fall through to the feature-flag write. Leave the stored value unread and don't migrate it.

No Waiting entry was settled by this change. Existing llm-and-prompts entries were tightened to fit the byte cap (6141/6144) and none were dropped. Checked and clean: no copies left beside the new constant, no unused imports introduced, no remaining doc or comment names the setting except the intentional history and retirement notes.

## Review — LIN-4393

Reviewed PR https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2377 at head `0e81c6c2c8d9535eee124d3d60bd5c107aba75ce` (base `3272fe4a6`). It is open and mergeable. Since then `main` has moved to `3bfa70b29`, which touches only `docs/reviews/**` and `docs/areas/front-end-pages.md`, so nothing overlaps this change.

CI: green on `0e81c6c2c`: Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, Secret scan (source) and CI success all passed.

### Against what was asked
- **"Settings no longer offers the setting."** Met. The Running row, the "Size policy set" row, the Undo row, `POST /settings/running/size-policy`, its undo sink, `loadSizePolicy`/`setSizePolicy`, the `settings-areas` feature and route entries, and the "Ready · larger/ask" state are all removed. Running reads `Runner ready` / `No runner`. A test confirms the testids are gone and the old route returns 404 with the stored preference left unchanged.
- **"Harbour keeps running hands-off … behaving as it does now with … 'err larger'."** Met. `STANDING_POLICY_LINE` (`lib/size-of-move.js`) is a constant, and scoping renders it on every path. The old no-policy `DECISION:` clause is gone. `size-policy-render.test.js` drives every scoping entrance (the dispatch-entrance override arm, proxy `/prompt`, proxy `/recommend?kind=scoping`, in-app prompt, routed input), each with no stored value and with a stored `ask`.
- **"Tidying that falls out of the removal is fine. Anything else goes to the area notes."** Met. The completion-signal wording, `survey.md` §How the choice is made, `source-map.md` and `ui-pieces.md` are updated. John's "per task breakdown" remark and the five hand-built prompt contexts are Waiting entries in `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`. No new tickets.
- **Not this ticket ("settings … for discussion").** Nothing was touched there.
- **"Done when … nothing that existed only for the setting remains."** Met. `git grep` on the PR head for `sizePolicy|loadSizePolicy|setSizePolicy|formatSizePolicyLine|SIZE_POLICIES|DEFAULT_SIZE_POLICY|size-policy|POLICY_MEANING|Ask each time` finds only:
  - the change-log retirement note and `SIZE_POLICY_WORDS`, kept on purpose so old rows still read;
  - the `workspace-preferences.js` "retired" note;
  - prompt change-log history and tests;
  - `docs/reviews/**` evidence, which is history and correctly untouched.
  `llms.txt` and `proxy-instructions.js` never named the setting.
- **Scope comment's extra condition (John's old row still reads and offers nothing broken).** Met. `SETTINGS` drops `sizePolicy`, `mergeChangeLog` marks retired rows not undoable, and `WorkspaceChangeLogStore.undo` refuses them `NOT_UNDOABLE` before `readCurrent`/`apply`. That closes the feature-flag fallthrough Survey open-0 #3 found. `preferences.sizePolicy` is left stored and unread, with no migration, as the PR states.
- **Kept, as required.** `DECIDED_BY` (all three values), every `SIZE_RECORD_*` guard including `SIZE_RECORD_POLICY_CUT`, the cut sentence ("the standing policy never decides one"), the size record, look-first and the selector fact. "The standing policy" wording is unchanged.

No narrowing. The implementation comment records no cuts, and I found none.

### Regression check
`git log` on the touched files shows only LIN-4368 (which added the setting), LIN-4369 replay arms and LIN-4370 look-first, plus older Settings work. LIN-4369 arm 4 wording ("scoping posts no comment", the record-shape lines) and LIN-4370's look-first sentence are intact in the scoping template. Nothing reverted is re-applied. Nothing in the ticket's paths changed after the ticket was created except through this PR.

### Mutation checks (LIN-2274), all reverted
- Deleted the store guard `if (!SETTINGS.includes(entry.setting)) throw … NOT_UNDOABLE` (`lib/workspace-change-log.js`). Red: "refuses NOT_UNDOABLE for a retired setting, before readCurrent or apply runs" and the route test "a forged Undo of the old row is refused not_undoable…".
- Dropped `SETTINGS.includes(r.setting)` from `mergeChangeLog`'s `undoable`. Red: "a change to a retired setting reads, and is not undoable" and "John's old change row still reads, with no Undo on the Change log or on Running".
- Put the old "no standing policy" line back in place of `STANDING_POLICY_LINE` in the scoping template. Red: all three proxy entrances, the override arm, the no-store render, and both `lin-4369-scoping-size-record` built-in-policy tests.

Local run of the 8 touched test files on the PR head: 150/150 pass.

### Isolated, or one of a class?
The class is a retired setting that still has logged history. `sizePolicy` is the only setting ever removed from `SETTINGS`, and the builder's new lesson in `docs/areas/auth-accounts-and-workspaces.md` records the pattern for next time. The other class is a context field threaded through the scoping renders by hand. That is the five hand-built contexts, already a Waiting entry in `llm-and-prompts.md`, and it is outside this ticket because John bounded it to the area notes. Otherwise the change is isolated.

### Leftovers
I agree with the builder's `### Leftovers`. The context-builder duplication is a Waiting note, the stale scoping-pointer note is tidied, and close-out has nothing to tidy. I found no other loose ends. `workspacePreferencesStore` is still used for other reads in every file that keeps it, and the only thing removed from `createPromptsRoutes` is the dependency it no longer reads.

### What CI Did Not Prove
- **Inside** (the setting's removal, the As-asked "Settings no longer offers the setting" plus the scope comment's old-row condition). **After the deploy:** open Settings › Running on the JKershaw workspace. There should be no "Size of the move" row and the sidebar should read `Runner ready`/`No runner`. On the Change log, John's 7 Nov row should read "Size of the move: err larger" with **no Undo button**. CI seeds this row's shape; only the live page shows the real stored row (`setting: 'sizePolicy', from: 'ask', to: 'err-larger'`).
- **Inside** (hands-off err-larger, the As-asked "a task runs hands-off without asking about size"). **After the deploy:** the next live scoping run on a fresh ticket should write a `## Size of the move` record with `Decided by: the standing policy` and raise no size `DECISION:` for a non-cut size. CI proves the prompt; only a live run shows the model follows it now that no workspace has a stored value to lean on.
- **Rollback:** revert the squash commit of #2377. That is safe because no data was migrated: `preferences.sizePolicy` is still stored, so the reverted code would read John's `err-larger` again.

### Verdict
Approve — conditional on close-out discharging the ledger

## Close-out — LIN-4393

**Merged:** [PR #2377](https://github.com/JKershaw/LinearViewer/pull/2377), squash commit `393c7686b860149c3f790d188544650ca901cd82`, pinned to head `0e81c6c2c8d9535eee124d3d60bd5c107aba75ce` with `--match-head-commit`. **Deployed:** harbour.cat's footer shows `393c7686b`.

**How it meets the ask:** see the review of 15:32. Settings no longer offers the setting. Scoping renders the built-in err-larger policy at every entrance. Nothing that existed only for the setting remains, apart from the history kept on purpose. Old rows still read but can't be undone.

**Changes I made after approval:** none. Review asked for no fixes and named no note entries. `main` had moved to `3bfa70b29`, which shares no files with the PR, so I merged without a rebase.

**Final CI:** green on `0e81c6c2c`. That covers Unit tests, E2E shards 1–4, the source secret scan and CI success. The PR state was `CLEAN` / `MERGEABLE`.

### Ledger
- **Inside: Settings › Running and John's Change log row, after the deploy. Not run.** *What:* on the JKershaw workspace, Running should have no "Size of the move" row and the sidebar should read `Runner ready` / `No runner`. John's 7 Nov row should read "Size of the move: err larger" with no Undo. *Why not run:* the page needs the owner's sign-in (`/workspace/jkershaw/settings/running` redirects 302 to `/`), and no proxy endpoint exposes it. *Who:* John, or anyone signed in to that workspace. This is also recorded on the PR.
- **Inside: the live scoping run is hands-off at err larger, after the deploy. Not run, with partial evidence.**
  - *Ran:* the live `GET /api/proxy/issues/LIN-4350/prompt/scoping` on `393c7686b` uses real workspace data and makes no model call. It renders `**Standing size policy:** err larger: …`. The old no-policy line is absent. "the standing policy never decides one" is kept, and `DECISION:` appears only for cuts.
  - *Not run:* what review named, which is the model's behaviour on a live run. That means a `## Size of the move` record reading `Decided by: the standing policy` on the next fresh-ticket, non-cut scoping run, with no size `DECISION:`. *Why:* no scoping run has started since the deploy. The latest, LIN-4382 at 15:22, ran before it. This session has no `dispatch` grant to start one. *Who:* the operator or autopilot, by reading the next scoping run's record. LIN-4346's review watches the same signal.
- **Rollback:** review's own, cited: revert squash commit `393c7686b`. `preferences.sizePolicy` is still stored, so the old code would read `err-larger` again.
- **Outside items:** none, so no follow-ups were filed. The leftovers already live as Waiting entries in `docs/areas/llm-and-prompts.md`, as John asked.

### Related tickets
- **LIN-4346** (blocked by this ticket) stays open. This ticket settles one item of its ledger, the standing-policy item, but LIN-4346 still has its own `implementation` step (the area notes pointer) and post-deploy checks. I left a comment there saying its blocker has landed.
- No rulings were raised.

relatedIssue.title: Deciding the size of the move becomes part of the run
